newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis up 1/2 in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis up 1/2 in thin trade.

text.p: Tax-exempts were quoted 1/2 point higher on Friday after debt futures and U.S. Treasuries gained in the face of the lowest unemployment rate in seven years, traders said.

Analysts said Treasury gains came from major short covering. Treasuries were volatile in early trade after the Labor Department said non-farm payrolls rose 250,000 in August and the unemployment rate fell to 5.1 percent from 5.4 percent.
The 30-year bond was quoted up 18/32 late Friday afternoon to yield 7.11 percent.
Back in the municipal market, some traders said improved bids were met with pulled offerings or blank stares and little trading took place.

Texas Turnpike five percent revenue bonds due 2025 reflected typical gains of Friday, one trader said. The bonds were bid at 5.91 percent late on Friday compared to a 5.95 percent bid at the close on Thursday.
The December municipal contract settled up 22/32 to 111-14/32, outpacing gains of 11/32 for the T-bond contract. The MOB spread widened to positive 150 from positive 139 at Thursday's close.

But George D. Friedlander, director of portfolio strategy at Smith Barney Inc, said the increase of dealer inventories from lows of $800-$900 million in August and anemic bond fund cash flows portend future underperformance for tax-exempts.
"The absence of significant institutional net demand raises the question of how long municipals can continue to sustain current valuations," Friedlander said in a recent publication.
In addition, he noted municipals are less attractive as their yields have declined as a percentage of Treasuries.
At least one trader at a large New York firm said there was a fair number of bonds sold away from the street. Thin trade was mostly a result of a lingering supply shortage, the trader said.

"The street is pretty light and we saw people putting good bids out there" the trader said. "We're coming off a period where there were no new issues so customers really don't have much to sell out the other side."
The Blue List of municipal offerings fell $45 million on Friday to $1.401 billion.
Looking ahead, traders said the mounting municipal new issue calendar should not pose a major hurdle for the market.
"There shouldn't be any problem with deals if they come in-line with the market because there hasn't been a lot to choose from," one trader said.

Next week's deals feature $324 million negotiated issue from Washington Public Power Supply System revenue refunding bonds via lead manager Goldman, Sachs & Co. The deal was lowered from $600 million because the general back-up in rates has prevented the utility from achieving desired savings targets, according to Goldman.

Other negotiated sales include $134 million Broward Co., Fla., revenue bonds via PaineWebber Inc; $100 million Wisconsin Health and Education revenue bonds via Merrill Lynch & co; and $139 million Sunrise, Fla., revenue bonds via William R. Hough & Co.
Competitive issues include $66.675 million Colorado Springs, Colo., revenue bonds on Monday.
The 30-day visible supply rose to $4.598 billion in Friday from $3.622 billion.
